intro: HR generalists often ask what do HR generalists make to ensure their own pay and their organization's compensation strategy remain competitive. This question highlights the broader challenge of salary benchmarking, a process that consumes significant time and requires precise data handling on your Mac.
tldr: Salary benchmarking is a manual, high-stakes task that often consumes one month of work per year for HR teams.
Avoid the title trap by focusing on job scope, responsibilities, and verified employer-reported data.
Use salary bands instead of fixed numbers to reduce the frequency of manual benchmarking exercises.

blocks.text: The real cost of manual salary benchmarking

When you ask what do HR generalists make, you are really asking about the value of market data. Benchmarking is not just a spreadsheet exercise. It is a strategic requirement. When done poorly, it leads to pay compression and talent loss. A single role takes half a day to price correctly. If you manage 50 roles, that is one month of your year gone. This is time you cannot spend on culture, development, or employee relations.
Why salary benchmarking causes HR burnout

The pressure to provide quick pay ranges often forces HR teams to use unreliable sources. Self-reported salary sites or unverified AI outputs can provide inflated numbers. This creates internal pay compression, where new hires earn more than tenured staff. Another major error is the title trap. You might match a role based on a title like Marketing Manager. However, the scope, reporting lines, and responsibilities might differ wildly from your internal role. This leads to unfair pay and legal risk.

items: Define roles by responsibilities, level, and scope instead of titles.
Prioritize verified, employer-reported salary surveys like Mercer, Radford, or WTW.
Build salary bands that span 20 to 40 percent to allow for growth.
Use integration-based platforms like Pave or Ravio to connect with your HRIS.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you manage your day

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It helps you handle the administrative side of HR work. Hold Option + Command to ask about anything on your screen. If you are lost in a complex Excel sheet, ask Lazur to explain the formula. If you need to find a specific setting in your HRIS, ask Lazur where it is. It will circle the button for you.
Using your Mac for compensation analysis

Most benchmarking happens in web browsers like Chrome or Safari. Use ⌘ + L to jump to the address bar quickly. If you are working in Excel on Mac, use ⌘ + ⌥ + V to paste values only. This keeps your data clean when moving numbers from a survey report into your internal tracker. Always check your employer's rules on handling sensitive employee or client data. Never upload PII to public AI tools.
Do not try to benchmark every role at once. Break it down into manageable chunks to keep your focus sharp.

faq.question: What do HR generalists make as a salary?
faq.answer: Salaries vary significantly based on company size, geography, and industry. Use verified, employer-reported surveys like Mercer or Radford to get accurate market data rather than relying on self-reported sites.

faq.question: How can I avoid the title trap in benchmarking?
faq.answer: Focus on the actual job content, including the level, scope of responsibility, and reporting structure, rather than just the job title.

faq.question: Is benchmarking on a Mac different than on Windows?
faq.answer: The core tasks are the same, but you should learn Mac keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + C and ⌘ + V to speed up your data entry in Excel or Google Sheets.
